hook: A company can collect thousands of complaints without recognizing that its product is the problem.
readerPromise: Understand how institutional attention can keep available information from becoming shared, actionable knowledge.
protectedRevelations: Later transition mechanisms and conclusions about collective correction
visualPlan: The information nobody recognizes: Let a pile of complaints grow while the product's design stays outside the company's named problem. Bring several private reports together under one newly shared description.

How reality becomes shared: Show which report gets a hearing, which label it receives and which observation is left aside. Move from one person's missed detail to separate institutions missing different parts of a situation.

Blindness inside successful work: Keep newsroom, ministry and laboratory each completing a task while one relevant fact remains outside it. Carry a private observation into a shared notice where others can recognize it.
Look at what remains unseen: Show the people and records carrying that notice, without any floating collective brain. End with existing evidence newly placed where a group can discuss it.

cueChanges.nextVisualChange: Keep complaint records accumulating beside an unchanged product category; no invented counts or metrics.
Use visible channels for a message to become shared, preserving differences in access.
Select one institutional task that highlights its target and leaves another observation outside attention.
End with the same overlooked evidence becoming a question, not a magically enlightened crowd.

sentenceIntentions.text: A company can collect thousands of complaints without recognizing that its product is the problem.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make plentiful complaints coexist with institutional blindness
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize information that fails to become an actionable problem

sentenceIntentions.text: Egregnosis gives a name to what a society becomes able to notice, share, and act on together.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Define egregnosis through collective noticing and action
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand the unfamiliar title as an observable social process

sentenceIntentions.text: It begins with what gets noticed, who gets heard, and which words make a problem recognizable.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Specify event selection, status and categories
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See concrete mechanisms behind public perception

sentenceIntentions.text: The book compares what individuals miss with the different pressures shaping what a society can notice.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Compare individual attention with collective pressures
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Expect careful analogy rather than a mystical group mind

sentenceIntentions.text: A newsroom, a ministry, and a laboratory can each miss something while performing their assigned task well.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Show competent institutions missing different things
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand blindness can arise without simple incompetence

sentenceIntentions.text: The question is how private knowledge becomes visible enough for people to act on together.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Ask how private knowledge becomes collectively usable
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel curiosity about the transition toward shared action

sentenceIntentions.text: There is no mysterious mind above society, just people and institutions deciding what becomes visible.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Make collective perception intelligible without supernatural imagery
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: See an observable inquiry into organization

sentenceIntentions.text: Begin with the things a society cannot see, especially when the evidence is already there.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Start from available evidence that remains unseen
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to inspect what a society's categories exclude

distinctiveContribution: Egregnosis names collective awareness as an observable product of attention, categories and channels, not a mind above society.
